claims.claim: Bumetanide, a 5-sulfamoyl anthranilic acid sharing the query acid-sulfamoyl core, has absolute oral bioavailability of 95% in cirrhosis patients after 1 mg oral versus IV dosing, and L2 context reports 95 to 100%.

The closest structural analog azosemide has L1 absolute oral bioavailability of 20.4% in fasted healthy humans, meeting the F >= 20% threshold; the L2 urinary-recovery estimate of 10% is indirect and does not overturn the L1 gold value.
Cirrhosis-condition contexts consistently show high oral bioavailability: metoclopramide 79 to 82% (L1) and 82% versus 60% control (L2), tolfenamic acid 91 to 100% (L1) and 113 to 126% (L2).
